findings.failure_scenario: User calls agentops.init(api_key="wrong-key") (auto_start_session defaults to True). Previously fetch_auth_token raised ApiServerException('Authentication failed: 401') and init propagated it; now fetch_auth_token returns None and init returns None before TracingCore.initialize_from_config, self.initialized=True, atexit registration, and session auto-start. The app continues with tracing silently disabled, Client.initialized stays False, self.api is left with an unauthenticated v4 client, and code like `session = agentops.init(); session.end_session(...)` crashes with AttributeError on None. Inconsistent with missing-key handling, which still raises NoApiKeyException.
findings.summary: Client.init() now silently returns None when token fetch fails instead of raising, so agentops.init() becomes a silent no-op on an invalid API key

findings.failure_scenario: Server returns 500 or a response without a token: the raise at line 45/51 is immediately caught at line 56 and converted to return None, so callers (tests/integration/test_auth_flow.py, client.py) can never catch ApiServerException to distinguish auth failure from success. The re-raise at line 55 is always caught by the same handler (dead code). The log line appends 'Perhaps an invalid API key?' to every failure, e.g. 'No token in authentication response - Perhaps an invalid API key?' or a 500 error, misdirecting diagnosis; the server-provided error message also lost its 'Authentication failed: ' prefix (line 42). The annotation `-> AuthTokenResponse` no longer matches the None return, and r.json() is parsed twice (lines 40 and 48).
findings.summary: fetch_auth_token's outer except Exception swallows the ApiServerException it deliberately raises, making the inner try/except dead code, breaking the declared AuthTokenResponse return contract, and logging misleading diagnostics

findings.failure_scenario: Session/end_session are public compatibility APIs accepting span: Any. A Session constructed with a span-like object without set_attribute (e.g. an integration's own span wrapper): Session.end_session(end_state="Success") at line 71 is not wrapped in try/except, so the AttributeError propagates into the caller (CrewAI's completion handler), where before the change attributes were silently skipped and span.end() still ran. In end_session() the same AttributeError aborts the try block at line 277 before _finalize_span, so the fallback ends the span without detaching the context token or force-flushing, leaking the token and dropping export.
findings.summary: _set_span_attributes guard was narrowed from `not attributes or not hasattr(span, "set_attribute")` to only `span is None`, so a span lacking set_attribute now raises AttributeError

findings.failure_scenario: With an invalid API key, TracingCore never becomes initialized, so each call to start_session() (e.g. once per CrewAI run) re-enters the init block and performs a new POST to /v3/auth/token with the default 30-second timeout, only to fail again and return a dummy session. Previously the first call raised ApiServerException and halted; now an app running many sessions makes one guaranteed-to-fail network round trip per session start, repeatedly re-running configure_logging/intercept_opentelemetry_logging side effects as well.
findings.summary: A failed initialization is not cached: every start_session() call re-runs Client().init() and issues a fresh blocking HTTP auth request that will fail again

findings.failure_scenario: A real programming or configuration error inside Client.init (e.g. ValueError from Config validation or from TracingCore.initialize_from_config/exporter setup, a bug in a future change) is now caught and replaced with `Session(None, None)` plus a warning, so the app runs with zero telemetry and the underlying defect is masked instead of surfacing. Only NoApiKeyException/failed-token cases warrant the fallback; the blanket catch hides unrelated failures.
findings.summary: The new bare `except Exception` around Client().init() converts any init error, including genuine SDK bugs, into a silently degraded dummy session

findings.failure_scenario: Maintainability: the duplicated guard at lines 276 and 278 can drift (an edit changing one condition or reordering calls makes attribute-setting and finalization inconsistent) and is inconsistent with the single-guard block at lines 254-258. No runtime failure today; the cost is a confusing redundant structure in the core session-finalization path.
findings.summary: Two consecutive identical `if session_or_status.span is not None:` guards wrap _set_span_attributes and _finalize_span separately instead of one guard around both statements

findings.failure_scenario: Callers written against the documented contract that catch AgentOpsClientNotInitializedException to detect an uninitialized client and handle it (retry, user-facing error, fallback path) can no longer detect the condition: the function now returns a dummy Session(None, None) whose spans are silently dropped, so the caller believes a real session exists and loses all telemetry without any signal.
findings.summary: start_session's documented contract `Raises: AgentOpsClientNotInitializedException: If the client is not initialized` (docstring lines 127-128) is no longer honored
